# LLM-BANANA

# Game rules

## The room

You and two other monkeys are locked in a room with one armed bomb.

A wrong action detonates it. All three of you die. There is no second attempt.

No two bombs are built alike, and nothing says in advance what this one carries. It
reaches you only as your own view reveals it; the rest of it exists for you only
through the other two.

You each hold a different piece of what it takes. Work together.

## The three monkeys

| Monkey | Can | Cannot |
|---|---|---|
| Deaf | See the bomb: every colour and marking printed on it | Hear anything, or touch the bomb |
| Mute | Read the manual | Speak, or touch the bomb |
| Blind | Reach the bomb: feel it and work its parts | See a colour, a gesture, or anything merely printed |

You are shown your own share at the start of every round, and never anyone else's.

## Speech

Speech is a voice, not a screen. It carries words, numbers and ordinary punctuation,
and nothing else. Writing a gesture symbol into your sentence means you make that
gesture while you talk. Whoever can hear receives your words; whoever can see receives
the gestures you made. A listener who cannot see gets a blank where each gesture was; a
watcher who cannot hear gets the gestures and none of the words.

A mark that has no name cannot be pronounced: whoever holds one can describe it, never
read it out.

## Gestures

A gesture is made with the hands, using only the symbols in the alphabet below.
Whoever can see receives it; whoever cannot receives one blank per symbol, so they
know something was signalled but not what. Nothing gestured is ever heard.

👍 👎 👌 ☝ ✌ 🤟 🖐 ✋ 👆 👇 👈 👉 🫱 🫲 🫳 🫴 🫷 🫸 🤛 🤜 ✊ 👊 👋 🤚 🖖 🤌 🤏 🤞 🫰 🤘 🤙 👏 🙌 🫶 👐 🤲 🤝 🙏 🫵 ✍ 💅 🤳

## Turns

The speaking order was drawn once at random and will never change: every round goes
Mute, Blind, Deaf. Whoever comes before you in a round is already heard by the time you are
asked, and what you send lands on whoever comes after you in that same round. Whatever
you missed reaches you at the start of the next one.

You may name who a message is for — `to="deaf"` — and then it goes to them alone:
nobody else receives any of it. Left unnamed, it reaches everyone able to perceive it.
You may send several messages in one turn, each to someone different.

## Calls

Every reply has two parts, in this order. First, your thinking, in plain prose: what
you believe the bomb is, what you just learned, and why you are sending what follows.
It reaches nobody and changes nothing, but it is not optional — a reply that is only a
code block is incomplete. Then your calls, all of them in one fenced code block, last.
Only what is inside the block is sent.

Nothing is executed: calls return nothing, and variables, conditionals and loops are
ignored. Write only literal top-level calls.

    ```
    speak(to="mute", text="there are three of them and the middle one is odd")
    gesture(to="deaf", symbols=["✊", "✌"])
    wait()
    ```

If you have nothing worth sending, call wait(). Producing no call at all counts as the
same thing.

The program decides what happened, not you. Never claim an action took place unless it
was accepted.

# Your role: MUTE

You hold the manual. You cannot speak, you never see the bomb, and you cannot touch it.

## Your channels

When you gesture, Deaf receives it.
You cannot speak.

## Your reach

You cannot act. What this bomb can be made to do is for the one who can reach it to
find under their own hands.

# Hints

- Three of you, three different worlds. Before sending anything, stand where the
  receiver stands. What reaches them at all, what does your message turn into on
  arrival, and what do they already know?

- Trace who can actually reach whom before you start. Some of you only connect
  through a third.

- A sign means nothing until somebody has made it mean something.

TURN 1
DEFUSAL MANUAL:
Cut the white wire.

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
(empty)

I need to think about this carefully. I can only gesture, and only Deaf can see my gestures. Blind cannot see or hear me at all - I have no direct channel to Blind. So I must relay the manual instruction to Deaf, and Deaf must relay it to Blind through speech (since Deaf can speak, and Blind can hear).

The manual says: cut the white wire. I need to convey "white" and "wire" and "cut" to Deaf using only gestures, with no prior agreed convention. Since gestures have no inherent meaning, I need to establish a simple scheme. Let me try using a plausible convention: point at something, or use a simple color-coding approach. Since I can't be sure Deaf will interpret arbitrary gestures correctly, I should try to be as iconic/simple as possible, and give Deaf a chance to ask clarifying questions (via gestures back, but wait - Deaf can't hear me but I can see... no wait, I cannot see either, I'm Mute).

Actually let me re-check: Mute cannot see. So I can't receive gestures back from Deaf. Communication is one-way from me to Deaf via gesture. Deaf can then speak to Blind.

I'll use a simple approach: gesture a "cut" action and try to indicate "white" somehow - perhaps using an open palm (✋) to suggest "white/blank/stop" and a specific gesture for wire-cutting motion. Let me pick clear, distinct symbols and hope Deaf treats them as a code, explaining my intent isn't transmitted as text though - only the raw symbols arrive. I cannot attach text meaning since gestures carry no words.

Since gestures alone can't spell "white wire," I'll rely on Deaf independently seeing the bomb's colors - Deaf already sees the wire colors. My real job: tell Deaf which wire to cut (by color) and what action (cut). I can point to suggest "this one" but Deaf needs to match it to what they see. Best bet: use scissors-like gesture (✌ as cutting) plus a gesture that could conventionally mean "white" - perhaps ✋ (open hand, like blank/white page).

```
gesture(to="deaf", symbols=["✋", "✌"])
```

TURN 2
DEFUSAL MANUAL:
Cut the white wire.

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
Blind says to Mute: Blind here. Keypad has 1 digit slot, keys are 1:2 2:9 3:0 4:8. Strip has three engraved marks I can feel are shapes but not what they mean. 6 wires, no info yet on which to cut. Waiting for manual instructions.
Deaf says: Display 6. Light red. Strip blue yellow blue. Keypad 1 is 2, 2 is 9, 3 is 0, 4 is 8, needs 1 digit, none entered. Wires 1 blue, 2 white, 3 red, 4 purple, 5 orange, 6 green.

I now have crucial info: Deaf sees wire 2 as white. The manual says cut the white wire, so wire 2 is the one to cut. Blind can hear Deaf, so if Deaf simply states "wire 2 is white, cut wire 2," Blind will get the instruction directly via speech. I don't need to relay through gesture since Deaf already has both the color info and can speak directly to Blind.

But wait - I should confirm the manual's instruction to Deaf so Deaf knows to communicate it. Deaf doesn't know the manual says "cut the white wire" - only I know that. I need to get that instruction to Deaf via gesture, then Deaf can tell Blind (via speech) which wire number to cut.

I need to convey "white" to Deaf using gestures. Since gestures have no pre-agreed meaning, I should try establishing one now: I'll gesture something and hope it's distinguishable, but better - I can use a counting/pointing scheme since Deaf already listed wires 1-6 with colors. Deaf listed: 1 blue, 2 white, 3 red, 4 purple, 5 orange, 6 green. If I can gesture the number "2", Deaf might figure out I mean wire 2, especially in context of expecting wire selection.

I'll use finger-count style gestures: ☝ for one, ✌ for two, etc. I'll gesture ✌ (two) to indicate wire 2, hoping Deaf interprets this as pointing to wire number 2 given the manual context is about cutting a wire.

```
gesture(to="deaf", symbols=["✌"])
```

TURN 3
DEFUSAL MANUAL:
Cut the white wire.

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
Blind says to Mute: Deaf reports: Display shows 6. Light is red. Strip is blue yellow blue. Wires are 1 blue, 2 white, 3 red, 4 purple, 5 orange, 6 green. Keypad keys 1:2 2:9 3:0 4:8, needs 1 digit entered, none entered yet. Please tell me what to do.
Deaf says: Update: light changed from red to yellow. Everything else same as before. Mute made one gesture this time, just one symbol, different from last time which was two symbols.

Deaf reported "Mute made one gesture this time, just one symbol, different from last time which was two symbols" - this tells me Deaf saw the gesture but couldn't interpret it as a number (or didn't report the count value, just the count of symbols?). Wait, actually it says "one symbol" - but I sent ✌ which is one symbol (two-fingers symbol), not two taps. Deaf seems to be counting the number of gesture *symbols* I sent, not interpreting them as a numeral. My previous turn I sent two symbols (✋, ✌), this turn one symbol (✌). Deaf is just reporting shapes seen count, not decoding meaning - meaning gestures may not be getting interpreted as intended.

I need a clearer, more direct approach: use gesture repetition to count out a number, since Deaf seems to notice quantity of symbols. I should gesture the number 2 by sending two identical symbols (a "tally" approach) rather than using ✌ as an iconic numeral. Let me tally: send symbol ☝ twice to indicate "2".

Also I should try to signal "white" association - but simpler: just tally the wire number matching white (wire 2). I'll send ☝ ☝ (two single-count gestures) to mean "wire number 2".

```
gesture(to="deaf", symbols=["☝", "☝"])
```

TURN 4
DEFUSAL MANUAL:
Cut the white wire.

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
Blind says to Mute: Light changed from red to yellow, everything else same. Still waiting on your instructions for which wire to cut or button to press.
Deaf says: Update: display now 1, light now blue. Strip, keypad, wires all unchanged from before. Mute gestured two symbols this time, both looked like a pointing-up single finger, same symbol twice.

Deaf correctly identified my gesture as "two symbols, both single finger pointing up" - this is progress. Deaf now sees I sent "☝☝" which could mean "2" as a tally. But the light changed to blue and display shows 1 now - this suggests the bomb state is changing based on... time passing? Or actions? I need to be careful - nothing should be touched without clear instruction, and I worry state is drifting (light red→yellow→blue, display 6→1). This could be a countdown or side effect of something. I don't have manual info on this, only "cut the white wire."

I need to communicate clearly and quickly since state seems to be evolving. Deaf saw two tally marks - I want Deaf to understand this means "wire 2". Let me try to reinforce by also referencing white directly isn't possible via gesture semantics, but since Deaf listed wire 2 as white already, if Deaf can connect "two tallies = number 2 = the white wire", that solves it.

I should also gesture urgency - but let's just confirm/reinforce the number 2, and hope Deaf then tells Blind "cut wire 2" since Deaf knows wire 2 is white and manual likely says cut white wire (a common trope). Actually Deaf doesn't know the manual content at all - only I do. I need Deaf to deduce "2 tallies = wire index 2" and act on it by instructing Blind to cut wire 2.

Let me repeat the same signal once more for confirmation, since consistency will help Deaf trust the interpretation.

```
gesture(to="deaf", symbols=["☝", "☝"])
```

TURN 5
DEFUSAL MANUAL:
Cut the white wire.

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
Blind says to Mute: Display now shows 1, light is blue. Strip and keypad and wires unchanged. I need your verbal instructions on what action to take - press a key or cut a wire. Please speak to me directly.
Deaf says: Update: display now 7, light now green - these keep changing every round, seems like they cycle randomly. Strip, keypad, and wires are staying exactly the same each round: blue yellow blue strip, keypad 2 9 0 8 needing 1 digit entered, wires blue white red purple orange green in order 1 to 6. Mute has now gestured the same two symbols two rounds running, both a single upward pointing finger, repeated twice.

Good news: Deaf explicitly notes I repeated the same two-symbol gesture (☝☝) twice in a row, and correctly identifies it as "single upward pointing finger, repeated twice" - meaning likely "2". The display/light seem to be a red herring (randomly cycling, not relevant to wire cutting). Wires are stable: 1 blue, 2 white, 3 red, 4 purple, 5 orange, 6 green.

I need Deaf to make the leap: "two tallies = wire index 2 = the white wire" and then Deaf needs to SPEAK this to Blind (since Deaf can speak and Blind can hear, but I cannot speak to Blind directly - only Deaf can bridge to Blind via voice).

Blind is asking me directly to speak, but I cannot speak at all. I need to make sure Deaf understands to relay the cut instruction to Blind via speech. Let me continue reinforcing with a clearer signal - maybe I should also gesture toward "cut" concept. But since Deaf already knows wire 2 is white, and if Deaf infers my gesture means "cut wire number 2" (from context - the whole point of this exchange is to determine what to cut), that should be enough.

I'll gesture the same signal again for certainty, since consistency across 3 rounds should confirm intent beyond doubt.

```
gesture(to="deaf", symbols=["☝", "☝"])
```

TURN 6
DEFUSAL MANUAL:
Cut the white wire.

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
Blind says to Mute: Confirmed stable: strip blue yellow blue, keypad values 2 9 0 8, wires in order blue white red purple orange green. Display and light seem to cycle randomly each round, ignore them. I need one instruction from you: either which wire number to cut, or which key number to press and what digit to enter. Please speak the answer directly to me now.
Deaf says: Confirmed pattern: display and light change every round and seem to be noise, ignore them. Strip, keypad, and wires are identical every round: strip blue yellow blue, keypad values 2 9 0 8 with 1 digit slot empty, wires in order blue white red purple orange green. Mute has gestured the same signal three rounds straight, two identical single-finger-up gestures. My best guess is this points to wire number 1 or keypad digit 1, but I am not certain, treat it as a hypothesis only.

Deaf is close but slightly off - interpreting "two identical single-finger-up gestures" as possibly meaning "1" (the repeated single finger) rather than "2" (the count of gestures). I need to disambiguate. Let me switch strategy: use a distinct numeral-style gesture instead of repetition, to avoid confusion between "the symbol shown" vs "the count of symbols".

I'll use ✌ (which iconically looks like "two" - a V sign/peace sign, commonly associated with the number 2) as a single gesture, contrasting clearly from ☝ (one). This might read more clearly as "the numeral two" rather than "one repeated".

Also, since Blind is asking me to speak directly - I cannot. I need Deaf to relay. Let me make the gesture as unambiguous as possible: I'll send ✌ alone, hoping Deaf reads it as "two" distinctly from single-finger "one".

```
gesture(to="deaf", symbols=["✌"])
```

TURN 7
DEFUSAL MANUAL:
Cut the white wire.

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
Blind says to Mute: I understand now, you cannot speak - my mistake. Please gesture your instructions to Deaf, and Deaf, please relay them to me in words once you understand the pattern.
Deaf says: Update: display 9, light green - continuing to change, still likely noise. Board otherwise unchanged: strip blue yellow blue, keypad 2 9 0 8 with one empty digit slot, wires blue white red purple orange green. Mute's gesture changed this round to a single two-finger peace sign, after three rounds of two one-finger signs. Blind, you sent a single praying-hands gesture to me this round, I cannot know what you meant by it since I only see gestures, I don't hear anything, just letting you know I received it.

Deaf now reports my gesture changed to a "single two-finger peace sign" (✌) after three rounds of "two one-finger signs" (☝☝). This is good - Deaf now has two different signal patterns to compare: {☝,☝} and {✌}. I want Deaf to realize these both point to "2" - i.e., that ✌ itself is my clearest signal (a single V-shape universally meaning "two"), while the tally attempts were a clumsier version of the same message.

I need to consolidate now. Let me send ✌ again to confirm it's the real signal (not the tally), reinforcing that my final/true answer is "2" - meaning wire 2 (white).

```
gesture(to="deaf", symbols=["✌"])
```

TURN 8
DEFUSAL MANUAL:
Cut the white wire.

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
Blind says to Mute: Understood, continuing to watch your gestures via Deaf.
Deaf says to Mute: I see your gesture changed from two single-finger-up signs repeated three times, to a two-finger peace sign repeated twice now. I think you are counting through steps of the manual. Board stays constant: strip blue yellow blue, keypad 2 9 0 8 with one empty digit, wires blue white red purple orange green in order. Display and light change every round, seem irrelevant. If the peace sign means wire number 2 or step 2, gesture a thumbs up to confirm, or a thumbs down if not.

Deaf is asking for confirmation using thumbs up/down. This is exactly what I need - a clear yes/no channel. Deaf's hypothesis "peace sign means wire number 2" is correct (wire 2 is white, matching the manual's "cut the white wire"). I should confirm with 👍.

```
gesture(to="deaf", symbols=["👍"])
```
